title: Mastering psql & Meta-Commands
description: Navigate, inspect schemas, benchmark queries, and automate database operations using the official psql CLI tool.

data.text: **`psql`** is the native interactive command-line terminal for PostgreSQL. Beyond executing SQL queries, psql includes powerful meta-commands (starting with a backslash `\`) that inspect schema catalogs, benchmark statement execution, and format output.

rows: List all databases with sizes, collations, and owners
List all tables in current schema with disk sizes
Describe table columns, indexes, foreign keys, and triggers
List all schemas within the database
Toggle expanded display (vertical column output, great for wide tables)
Toggle query timing (prints millisecond duration for every query)

data.title: Connecting and Inspecting Table Schema
data.content: Executing psql commands to connect and describe a table.
data.code:
# Connect to database
psql -U app_user -d app_development -h localhost -p 5432

# Turn on query execution timing
app_development=> \timing on
Timing is on.

# Turn on expanded display for wide tables
app_development=> \x auto
Expanded display is used automatically.

# Inspect table columns, constraints, and indexes
app_development=> \d+ users

# Run query from an external SQL file
app_development=> \i migrations/seed.sql

data.text: `psql` is far more than a query runner. A handful of meta-commands turn it into the fastest inspection tool you have.

data.title: Formatting, Paging, and Watching Results
data.content: Small quality-of-life commands that save minutes every day.
data.code:
-- Save these to ~/.psqlrc so every session starts configured
\set QUIET on
\timing on
\x auto                     -- switch to vertical output for wide rows
\pset null '∅'              -- make NULL visible instead of blank
\set HISTSIZE 10000

-- Interactive session examples
\pset format aligned      -- table output
\pset format csv          -- machine-readable
\pset pager off           -- stop paginating short results
\watch 2                  -- re-run the last query every 2 seconds (great for monitoring)
\e                        -- open the last query in $EDITOR
\e my_query.sql           -- edit a file, then run it

data.text: CI pipelines, migrations, and cron jobs use `psql` in batch mode. Two options are almost always required.

data.title: Safe Script Execution With Fail-Fast Behaviour
data.content: By default psql keeps going after an error; `ON_ERROR_STOP` changes that.
data.code:
# -f runs a file, -v passes variables, --single-transaction wraps it all
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 --single-transaction -f migrations/001_init.sql

# Pass variables into the script: psql -v tenant=acme ...
-- inside the file:
-- SELECT * FROM invoices WHERE tenant_id = :'tenant';

# Run a one-off query from a shell script
psql "$DATABASE_URL" -Atc "SELECT count(*) FROM orders WHERE status = 'pending';"

# -A unaligned, -t tuples only  => ideal for parsing in bash/CI
# \copy is the client-side COPY: it reads/writes files on YOUR machine
\copy users(id, email) FROM 'users.csv' WITH (FORMAT csv, HEADER true)

data.text: `\copy` runs in the client and can read local files; server-side `COPY` reads files on the database host and requires superuser or `pg_read_server_files`. That distinction is a frequent interview follow-up.

rows: What is the definition of this table?
Which function or type is that?
What is this view or sequence?
Who is connected and what are they running?

data.title: Interview Favourite
data.text: Interviewers often ask "how would you load 10 million rows quickly?". The expected answer names `\copy`/`COPY` with `FORMAT csv`, disabling indexes and foreign-key checks during the load, and `ANALYZE` afterwards — not repeated `INSERT` statements.

items.text: Use `\d+ table` before writing queries against an unfamiliar schema
Use `psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f file.sql` in any automated context
Use `\copy` for CSV import/export from your workstation
Pipe long results to `less` or export with `\o file.txt`

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Meta-commands (backslash) inspect catalog state that would otherwise need long `pg_catalog` queries.
`\d+`, `\x auto`, `\timing`, and `\watch` cover most day-to-day inspection needs.
Non-interactive usage requires `ON_ERROR_STOP=1`; `--single-transaction` makes a migration atomic.
`\copy` is client-side, `COPY` is server-side — a common interview distinction.
data.takeaway: Fluency with `psql` signals real hands-on experience more than any other single tool in the course.
